Nem Nuong is delicious; cleanliness and service not so much
Oct 2019
If you have never tried Nem Nuong then you should. Grilled pork on a skewer, wrapped in greens and rice paper, then dipped in a flavorful peanut(?) sauce, is so good that it is very easy to overeat. 

Service is fast but not particularly helpful as they seem to be most interested in turning tables. English is not really spoken here so the lack of help can lead to less than complete enjoyment of a wonderful dish. Anyway, 

The place is not so clean but the customers don't help matters much when tossing napkins, food, etc. onto the floor. The greens seem to be washed thoroughly so unless you have a fragile stomach, should not be any post-meal issues.

Would love to give 5 stars but the ambiance and service shortcomings can't be dismissed. Still it is a truly local place with an iconic dish so worth visiting if in Dalat, tired of hotel food, and a bit adventuresome. Typically, taxi drivers will wait so can bring you back to your hotel if that is a concern.

Amazing Food with Complimentary Ride to Bus Station:)
Apr 2019 • Friends
Ok, this place. Wow. The BBQ man was there ALL day, and the staff was in the back ALL day making skewers to grill. The service was fast, not that I cared, and damn these rolls of goodness were unreal. It was packed with locals and just humming as it was the big long weekend (Reunification Day). The rice paper has a tougher texture to it that the greens moisten up and the papers tugs and gives way to the fresh lettuces and crunchy bits and grilled pork. The sauce was great - I added a fair bit of chilli. Oh i asked the owner to call me a Grab (Uber), but she said they were not many around, so she drove me to the bus station. Typical South Vietnam hospitality. A highlight meal for sure of a great trip.

Local Recommended!
Nov 2018 • Friends
My friends and I visited Da Lat last weeekend. We originally intended to have lunch at another local vietnamese restaurant but the place was close. We had no idea where to find good local meal, so we asked our driver for recommendation. He said Ba Hung is a good choice.

Although none of the staff speak a word of English, the fact that they have just one menu makes it simple enough for us to order food. You just need to tell them how many serving of 'nem noung' you need. The cost is VND45,000 for a serving.

Four of us order 2 at first, the red meat is served with this crispy thingy (I think it's crackling) and loads of veggies. There's also flour sheet and peanut-y dipping sauce on a side. What you have to do is spread out the flour sheet, top with some green, put in some meat and crackling, roll it up, and voila!

The first bite was a bit confusing for all of us as we're more familiar with the 'adapted' taste of vietnamese food in Thailand. But I can say for sure that we finished the two serving within like 10 minutes. And still wanted more.

We decided to order one more serving to share. Since nobody there speaks English, it took us about 15 minutes until we get more food. The lady thought we want to check, when in fact we actually want more food. We almost gave up and got the bill instead of having more nem noung. Luckily, one of my friends did some body language signing 'we want more' and the lady somehow got it at the end, so she went to the back and brought us more food.

The service is great despite the language barrier. The food is pretty tasty too. There're people walking in almost all the time we sat there. The price is very very affordable too. I recommend if you want some local food experience, Ba Hung is one of the place you shouldn't miss.
